metadata.title: Exploration of Variables Predicting Sense of School Belonging Using the Machine Learning Method—Group Mnet

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2015 microdata for Korean students and merges multiple PISA questionnaires (student background, ICT familiarity, educational career, and parent) before modeling. In the preprocessing stage, the authors explicitly removed weighting-related variables (e.g., W_FSTURWT) from the candidate predictors, but the manuscript does not state whether PISA sampling weights were applied in estimation or evaluation. Because the analysis is based on group Mnet penalized regression with k-NN imputation, the paper does not describe any complex-survey variance estimation or replicate-weight use. Therefore, readers should treat the reported prediction error (RMSE) as coming from an analysis that may not incorporate PISA complex-sampling weights, and should consider re-running with appropriate PISA weights if population-representative inference is required.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Analytic dataset was constructed from PISA 2015 for Korea by merging four questionnaires (student background, ICT familiarity, educational career, and parent) to start with 927 student+parent variables. Variables were removed if irrelevant to analysis, including identification variables (e.g., CNTSTUID), weighting variables (e.g., W_FSTURWT), and administration variables (e.g., ADMINMODE). For plausible values, only the first PV of each subject was retained and the other PVs were deleted. Variables with ≥30% missingness were deleted (68 variables), near-zero variance variables were removed (65 variables), and derived variables (e.g., ANXTEST, MOTIVA) were removed and replaced by individual items, yielding 504 candidate variables. For missingness among remaining predictors, listwise deletion retained only 454/5581 (~8.13%), so k-NN imputation was applied using k=40 (sqrt of 1638 complete cases) with Gower distance to handle mixed variable formats.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2015 (Korea), student sense of school belonging (4-point Likert, ST034)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Group Mnet prediction error (test RMSE) stable across 100 random splits: RMSE range 0.36–0.41, mean 0.39 (SD = 0.009). Model selected on average 74.55 variables (SD = 22.14) out of 504 per run; 32 variables were selected in ≥75 iterations and interpreted.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2015 (Korea) the study leveraged student gender, perceived school safety (threatened by other students), teacher treatment (graded harder), parental support, and life satisfaction to predict students’ sense of school belonging, finding that safer school climates, fairer teacher treatment, and supportive home relationships were associated with higher belonging while threat/victimization and anxiety-related items were associated with lower belonging. This indicates that interventions targeting school climate and student–teacher/peer relationships—alongside family emotional support and students’ well-being—may be more actionable for improving belonging than relying on a narrow set of traditional predictors, though the study is predictive and does not establish causal effects.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzed PISA 2015 data for Korea (N=5,581 students) to predict students’ sense of school belonging measured by a 4-point Likert scale (ST034). After extensive variable screening (removing identification/weighting/administration variables, keeping only the first PV per subject, deleting variables with ≥30% missingness, and removing near-zero-variance and derived variables), the authors used k-NN imputation for remaining missing predictor values and then applied group Mnet (a penalized regression with nonconvex MCP plus ridge) to search among 504 candidate predictors. Model performance was evaluated via repeated random train/test splits (7:3) with 10-fold CV on training and 100 iterations; test RMSE was stable (mean RMSE=0.39, SD=0.009; range 0.36–0.41). The most consistently selected predictors (32 variables selected in ≥75 iterations) spanned school climate, peer/teacher relationships, parental support, motivation/anxiety, ICT attitudes, and learning/physical activities. Limitations include the lack of explicit PISA complex-survey weight application reporting and the fact that penalized selection/importance supports prediction rather than causal inference.
